area: master chain / first sound after the context is made
problem: The very first sound after the AudioContext is created comes out up to 9.8 dB quieter, because Chrome's glue compressor is cold. AUDIO.md 3.7 describes this warm-up but says the engine's long-lived context has no such problem. It does for the first sound. wire.js unlocks on pointerdown, touchend and keydown (wire.js 344-355), and the sound of the key press or touch that unlocked plays in the same task, 12 ms after the context starts. A mouse click comes about 60 to 150 ms after its pointerdown, so a mouse-first player loses only 0.4 to 2.8 dB. A keyboard-first or touch-first player gets the loss in full.
evidence: Real engine, same sound in its own context: ui.tick#light K Fast -43.3 dB first versus -33.5 later (-9.6 to -9.8 dB), peak -24.5 versus -13.3 dBFS. ui.select#i0 -8.9, world.step#a -8.5, ui.toggle#on -5.2, draft.pick#slot2 -4.9, ui.ok -2.5, sale.win -2.6. Delay after context start versus the 3 s level, ui.tick#light: 0 ms -9.6, 60 ms -2.8, 100 ms -1.3, 150 ms -0.4, 250 ms 0. 44.1 kHz gives -9.85. Priming the chain with a -80 dBFS sine, a -100 dBFS sine or a zero-gain source changed nothing (-43.3 in all five), so the cause is elapsed time since the compressor started, not signal history.
fix: In engine.js, record the time the context was created and, in mix(), set startT = max(startT, createdAt + 0.15) while ctx.currentTime is under 0.15. This delays only the first sound, once. Alternatively apply a one-off gain of about +10 dB falling to 0 over 150 ms to a voice that starts in that window, and correct the sentence in AUDIO.md 3.7. Add a render check that plays at currentTime 0 and holds the result within 1 dB of the same sound at 1 s.

area: repair dial tone level on a quiet laptop (engine dialApi)
problem: The dial tone is the only non-visual way to play the repair timing game, but its low notes are barely played on the 40-phon laptop model. It is level in K-weighting (flat sine, -33 dBFS peak) with no loudness compensation across its D4 to D6 range. Through a 220 Hz high-pass plus A-weighting the D4 to A4 half of the dial lies below the quietest tiny sound, and the level varies by 8.8 dB across the dial. The tone has no recipe, so no level check covers it.
evidence: Steady-state A-weighted Fast after the high-pass, marker out of the green zone, D4 to D6: -44.5, -43.2, -42.0, -40.5, -39.6, -38.5, -37.8, -37.3, -36.5, -36.2, -35.7 dB (identical at 44.1 and 48 kHz). K Fast is flat at -36.2 to -35.0. Tiny tier: median -33.5, quietest -37.2. D4 to A4 are 3.3 to 7.3 dB under the quietest tiny sound; D4 is 11 dB under the tiny median. Inside the zone D4 is -39.2 (still 2 dB under the quietest tiny sound) and D6 -32.0. Start and stop are click-free (end step -79.5 dBFS).
fix: Tilt the tone's gain by note to equal laptop loudness: about +8 dB at D4, +6 at E4, +4 at F#4, +2 at A4, tapering to 0 at D6. The sine peaks at -33 dBFS, far under the -6 tiny ceiling. Or keep the octave partial (currently 0.0001 outside the zone) at about -6 dB for notes below A4. Add a render test holding every dial note within 3 dB of the tiny median on the A-weighted Fast model.

problem: Run-scoped resolver state is never reset when a game is left, so one run's state leaks into the next. A manager's coin held while a dialog was open rings as a loud XL coin shower at the first dialog close of the NEXT run. The 'first three door bells of a run always ring' rule (fourth round, W-3) only holds for the first run of a page load.
evidence: Cause: `unwire()` (wire.js:516) calls `audio.release()` (engine.js:484), which sets `env.hold=false` but never resets `rs` (holdNet, holdAny, fastNet, buyers, days, states). `go()` (main.js:28,31) runs the cleanup, which unwires, before `dlg.close()`. The dialog observer's `audio.hold(false)` (wire.js:424, engine.js:453 `if (env.hold === on) return`) then returns early, so `holdRelease` never runs and the sum stays. Only audition.js:82 ever re-creates the resolver state. Real page (scratchpad/ar2-wire-3/probe7.mjs, out7.txt): game, open Menu, `pc.S.game.emit('cycle',{zone:1,net:250000,pid:1})` (it reads holdNet=250000 holdAny=true), Start over, new Draft, Begin. Help opened and closed in run 2: the log shows `ui.dialog-close#d [tiny]` and `cash.in#xl [loud]` at 14522 ms, and holdNet reads 0 again. Engine level (stale.mjs): release() leaves holdNet 250000, then the next hold(true) and hold(false) plays `cash.in`. Door bells (buyers.mjs): run 1 plays 3 bells, `release()`, run 2's first three `buyer.arrive` requests 7 to 15 s later give played=3 total and dropped={budget:3}, with resolver.buyers still 3. Academy lessons are wired like games (wire.js:486 comment) and `buyer.*` is not in SANDBOX_SILENT, so the Academy probably spends the three teaching bells before a first-time player's real run (inferred from the code, not run).
fix: Reset the run-scoped fields when a real (non-sandbox) game is wired or left. For example, in `wireGame` for `!sandbox`, `Object.assign(rs, { holdNet:0, holdAny:false, fastNet:0, nextFast:0, buyers:0, days:0, states:{}, lastCycle:-Infinity, lastBuyer:-Infinity, lastUrgent:-Infinity })`, and in `release()` clear holdNet, holdAny and fastNet. Keep the reward-budget fields. The reset must live in the engine or `wireGame` because `createResolverState` is not exported through audio/index.js. Add a test: hold, request cycle, release, hold(true), hold(false) must play nothing.

area: Screen-reader and switch users: audio unlock
problem: The page unlocks audio only on pointerdown, touchend and keydown. A bare click, which is how assistive technology's default action usually reaches a page, never creates the audio context. The game stays silent: no ticks, no first-run hint, no dial tone. The Dial tone switch in the Deal Room, the only non-visual way to time a repair, cannot start it either. Only the 'Play a test sound' button unlocks the engine, and a screen-reader user has no reason to find it.
evidence: js/audio/wire.js line 355 binds unlock to ['pointerdown','touchend','keydown']; the click capture handler only calls audio.touch(). In Chrome I sent two clicks with user activation (userGesture, navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive true) and no pointer or key event, on Play solo and then on a Draft card. Result: {state:'locked', played:{}, dropped:{locked:2}}, toasts []. That AT sends a bare click, and grants activation with it, is inferred from how Chromium's accessibility default action works. I did not run NVDA, JAWS or VoiceOver.
fix: Also unlock on trusted 'click' (keep the isTrusted === false skip) and on pointerup, or call audio.unlock() in the click capture handler when audio.state is 'locked'. Add a test that sends only a click. Then check once with NVDA in browse mode plus Chrome, and VoiceOver. If it reproduces there, treat it as a blocker.

area: Classroom path: a student who has ever touched sound
problem: A student whose saved settings have touched:true (a volume nudge, key M, or a preset chosen in any earlier session in that browser) joins the room with their own mix. They get no Classroom, no toast and no sound note anywhere in the Draft. Their Begin fanfare plays at full volume. FACULTY_KIT step 2 still tells the class 'sound is quiet in a room', so for these students it is not true and nobody tells them. The instructor cannot see who is affected.
evidence: A second page opened with ?room=... and settings {master:80, touched:true, hinted:true}. After Join: toasts [] and audio unchanged (quiet:false, master:80). After Begin: toasts [], played {ui.tick, draft.pick x2, draft.begin}. The Draft text has no sound line. AUDIO.md H.2 lists the volume-counts-as-touched asymmetry as open. COMPLIANCE and the kit describe it as a limit, but the five-minute setup does not mention it.
fix: Do not let a bare volume change set touched. For a touched student who joins a room, show one note: 'Your own sound settings stay in this room (Full, 80 percent). Press M to mute, or choose Classroom (quieter) under Display and sound.' Change the kit's class script to 'press M now, or use headphones', which is true for everyone.

area: Instructor with a room of 40: no silent option, Classroom still plays fanfares
problem: The dashboard offers one sound choice, 'Quiet sound link', which means Classroom: the tiny game sounds and the clock sounds are off and everything else is 6 to 8 dB lower. A lab or lecture hall full of Classroom laptops still gets level-up fanfares and sale registers all period. Deploying a shock makes every student's laptop play the loud alert and the level-up fanfare at the same moment. ?sound=off exists in code but is in neither the dashboard nor the kit.
evidence: Real two-page room, student in Classroom, instructor presses Deploy (Fed): the student's engine requested level.up, achievement, codex x2 and alert.shock, and played {alert.shock:1, level.up:1} with dropped {quiet:3}. Those are two loud-tier sounds at about 12 dB under Full. The audition page's typical minute plays 40 sounds in Full and 24 in Classroom (16 held back by 'quiet'). Per-run reward counts are in AUDIO.md 3.4.4. settings.js fromAddress() already handles sound=off. FACULTY_KIT says Classroom is 'about 12 dB under full', which is not a number an instructor can use.
fix: Turn the checkbox into 'Sound in the student link: Normal / Quiet / Off'. Make Off a room-scoped mute that is given back on leaving, like the room rule, and not a permanent touched mute. In Classroom, play a soft or tick-only version of the loud reward fanfares (level.up l and big, epic achievement, milestone) and of alert.shock. Say in plain words in the kit that Classroom is 'less than half as loud, and still not silent'.

area: Audition page: navigation under the sticky bar
problem: Every contents link scrolls its section so that the heading, the blurb and the 'Play all N' button sit under the 160 px sticky control bar. The author lands on card tails with no title and has to scroll up each time. The bar permanently covers about a fifth of a laptop screen. The contents list itself scrolls away, so on a 16,000 px page there is no quick way back to it.
evidence: At 1366x768, after the Refusals link: h2 top 0, bar bottom 160, and a screenshot shows only card bottoms. The bar is 160 px of 768, and 275 px of 800 at 390 px wide. #toc has position static. Page height is 16,443 px with 397 buttons.
fix: Add section.grp { scroll-margin-top: 170px } (or html { scroll-padding-top } read from the bar's height). Make the contents a sticky one-line strip or add a 'Contents' link inside the bar. Let the bar collapse its checkbox row.
